```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Trino is an open-source SQL query engine that connects to other data
stores. Starburst Enterprise builds on Trino. Use a self-hosted Trino cluster or Starburst Enterprise as a data source for Shiny.
People sign in with the cluster's identity provider and query using their
own database permissions.

You can run Trino and its trusted OAuth identity provider on your own
infrastructure. The installed package includes a local Trino and Keycloak
demo, described below.

The connection uses RTrino, so you can write queries with DBI or dbplyr.

## Set up sign-in

Run `install.packages("RTrino")` in R (version 0.1.0 or later).
Ask the cluster administrator for an OAuth
app registration the cluster accepts, with `http://localhost:8100` as its
redirect URI.

You'll need the registration's client ID and secret, and the sign-in
provider's issuer URL. This example uses the person's profile email as the
Trino username; check that this matches the cluster's user mapping.

Save these values in a local `.Renviron` file and restart R:

```text
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret
OAUTHDB_TRINO_ISSUER=https://your-identity-provider.example.org
```

Try `shinyOAuthDB::oauth_db_demo("trino")` for a local cluster, sign-in and
sample data. See [Local Docker demos](local-demos.html) for accounts and cleanup.

| Setting | Where to get it |
| --- | --- |
| `host` | The coordinator's HTTPS URL and port from your cluster administrator |
| `catalog` | The data source name shown by Trino's `SHOW CATALOGS` |
| `schema` | A schema listed by `SHOW SCHEMAS FROM your_catalog` |
| Issuer, client ID, secret | The cluster's trusted provider and your [Shiny client registration](oauth-setup.html) |
| User field | The profile claim selected by the cluster's principal mapping |

Ask the administrator to check OAuth and impersonation rules as described
after the app example. A cluster's own Web UI registration may have a
different audience from the Shiny app.

## A complete app

Save this as `app.R`. Replace the cluster URL, catalog, and schema, and
use the scopes your registration allows:

```{r app}
library(shiny)
library(shinyOAuth)
library(shinyOAuthDB)

provider <- oauth_provider_oidc_discover(
  issuer = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_TRINO_ISSUER")
)
client <- oauth_client(
  provider,
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100",
  scopes = c("openid", "profile", "email", "offline_access")
)

ui <- oauth_ui(fluidPage(
  actionButton("login", "Sign in"),
  actionButton("logout", "Sign out"),
  tableOutput("rows")
), id = "auth", client = client)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  auth <- oauth_module_server("auth", client, auto_redirect = FALSE)
  observeEvent(input$login, auth$request_login())
  observeEvent(input$logout, auth$logout())

  con <- oauth_db_trino(
    auth$connection,
    host = "https://trino.example.org",
    catalog = "lakehouse",
    schema = "reporting",
    user = function() req(auth$token@userinfo$email)
  )
  output$rows <- renderTable({
    connection <- con()
    DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT current_user")
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server, options = list(port = 8100), uiPattern = ".*")
```

Run `shiny::runApp(port = 8100)` from the app directory and open
`http://localhost:8100`. Sign in to run the query; signing out clears the
output.

The query shows the Trino user. Replace it with SQL for your data.
`con()` returns the DBI connection; call it inside the render or reactive
expression before using DBI or dbplyr.

## Prepare the coordinator and identity provider

The local demo contains `trino/etc/config.properties` and an access-control
policy you can inspect with `oauth_db_demo("trino", action = "files")`.
For your coordinator, configure HTTPS and its OAuth provider. The relevant
settings include:

```text
http-server.authentication.type=oauth2
http-server.authentication.oauth2.issuer=https://login.example.org/realms/reporting
http-server.authentication.oauth2.client-id=your-coordinator-client
http-server.authentication.oauth2.client-secret=your-coordinator-secret
http-server.authentication.oauth2.additional-audiences=your-shiny-api-audience
http-server.authentication.oauth2.principal-field=email
```

The coordinator's OAuth client is separate from the app's registration.
Both must agree on the access-token issuer and accepted audience. The app
uses the profile email for `user`; change both sides if your deployment
uses a different claim. With locally verifiable JWTs, check whether
`http-server.authentication.oauth2.oidc.use-userinfo-endpoint=false` is
appropriate for your issuer. See [Trino OAuth configuration](https://trino.io/docs/current/security/oauth2).
Configure access control to restrict impersonation, catalogs and tables;
authentication alone doesn't define data permissions.

## Connection settings

Include the HTTPS port in `host`, or pass `port` separately. Set
`ca_bundle` if the cluster uses a private CA. Other options, such as
`timeout` and `query_max_run_time`, go to RTrino; see `?oauth_db_trino`.

RTrino gets a current token for each request, including result pages.
The connection stays open through ordinary token refresh and closes on
account changes, sign-out, or session end.

## Match the cluster's sign-in configuration

The cluster must trust access tokens from your app's issuer and audience,
and map the token's principal to a Trino user. A successful sign-in to the
cluster's web UI alone doesn't establish this for your Shiny app.
See [Trino's OAuth configuration](https://trino.io/docs/current/security/oauth2.html)
for the server settings.

The `user` argument must match that mapping. Use a function to read the
username from the selected account, as in the app above. If your provider
uses another verified profile field, replace `email` with that field.
The helper creates a new connection when the username changes.

Starburst Galaxy needs its own OAuth registration and endpoint setup.
For saved query results, see
[Authentication and sessions](authorization.html).
